title: Redwood discovery - model selection (Rivermark AI)
summary: Intro discovery to understand Rivermark's model selection needs across hosted/dedicated/private. Key topics: multilingual support, large context (>=64k), tool-calling/function-calling, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed to run benchmarks on 3 open models and share pricing + security pack.
topics: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (CTO, Rivermark), Priya Kapoor (ML Eng, Rivermark), Marco Ruiz (Infra/Sec)

[00:00] Jenna: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jenna from redwood, i'm the ae on this account, i'll hand over to samir who will do a quick technical rundown and then we can jump into your requirements.
[00:18] Samir: thanks jenna. hi liam, priya, marco, good to meet you. Quick agenda: model selection tradeoffs, context window needs, multilingual, tool-calling/function calling, and security implications for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:35] Liam: yep sounds good. quick background: Rivermark builds a customer support assistant that ingests long ticket histories and call transcripts, lots of spanish and portuguese traffic, sometimes french. We're hitting concat windows of 60k+ tokens for deep thread summarization and RAG.
[00:55] Priya: and we also have vector DB + retrieval pipeline, but we'd like the model to support function calls so it can invoke internal tools (ticket lookup, create follow-up). latency target is p95 < 600ms for simple turn, but for long context summarization we accept higher.
[01:20] Marco: security is huge — we need VPC, KMS for keys, audit logs, SSO/SAML and SOC2 or equivalent. Also data residency in EU for EU customers.
[01:40] Samir: great — that's helpful. On context windows: Redwood has hosted models and we also serve larger-context open models on Dedicated/Private. For 64k+ we typically recommend Dedicated or Private because it gives more control over kernel selection and memory configs; Hosted can support some 32k variants but there are cost/latency implications.
[02:05] Priya: does Redwood host any open models with 64k out of the box? or would we need Dedicated?
[02:12] Jenna: today Hosted catalog includes curated open weights up to 32k comfortable; for 64k we usually do Dedicated or Private stacks, or we can run a dedicated hosted pool for enterprise — there's a tradeoff on cost.
[02:30] Liam: got it. can you explain the tradeoffs — latency and cost — for 32k vs 64k and quantization choices?
[02:42] Samir: sure. larger context increases memory pressure so you either increase GPU memory (bigger instances) or use KV caching and offloading. Quantization (4-bit/5-bit) can reduce memory but sometimes impacts quality on generation, especially on multilingual tokenization. Redwood's runtime tries to pick kernels and quant profiles per model; on Dedicated you can pin quant profiles for your workload. There's also batching effects — for small latencies we reduce batching and use sticky routing.
[03:15] Marco: you mentioned KV cache — is that the K-V cash? excuse me — K v cache? how's that persisted and does it leak across tenants?
[03:23] Samir: yeah sorry transcription, K-V cache. It's per-request or per-session and in Dedicated we can enable customer-isolated caches; in Hosted it's ephemeral but logically isolated. We also support prefix caching to reduce repeated context costs.
[03:40] Priya: about multilingual — how do you evaluate? we found a lot of models skew toward english; any bench for spanish/pt?
[03:48] Samir: we run evals on language-specific benchmarks, and Redwood Optimize suggests model+quant profiles per workload. For example Mistral and Mistral variants do well on european languages, and some Llama-derivatives with recent finetunes show improved tokenization for spanish/pt. We'll propose 3 models to benchmark with your sample prompts.
[04:10] Liam: can you name the models you'd suggest? we prefer open weights or permissive licenses.
[04:15] Jenna: top picks: 1) Mistral X-ish open variant (we'll confirm exact repo), 2) a Llama 3 community variant with 32/64k configs, 3) an LLM optimized for multilingual e.g. x-xx model — we'll send exact names and perf numbers. Competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI are also options but you said you prefer open models.
[04:45] Marco: on private deployment — what's required from our infra side? we are air-gapped for some EU customers sometimes.
[04:53] Samir: Private (on-prem) needs network access for initial install, we support an air-gapped bundle. For VPC deployments we provide a control plane option that talks over a customer-managed VPC peering with encrypted channels; KMS integration is via customer KMS or HSM. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[05:20] Priya: function calling — is Redwood's function-calling compatible with our existing toolchain? we have internal APIs with JSON schemas.
[05:28] Samir: yes we support structured outputs and function-calling semantics. We also have streaming responses + function call hooks so the model can emit a function call, you run it, and then continue the conversation. Some community models need small wrapper layers to get robust JSON output; we can layer mild RLHF or output validators in the pipeline.
[05:50] Liam: do you support custom tool registries or is it just ad-hoc?
[05:54] Samir: you can register tools in the Redwood console and assign RBAC. In Dedicated/Private you get deeper integrations and can run tool executors inside your VPC.
[06:10] Priya: latency for function-calling flows — if model triggers a tool call and waits, how do you recommend designing it to keep p95 under 1s?
[06:18] Samir: common pattern: async tool invocation with streaming; model emits an intent quickly, you return a lightweight ack and then either stream the final answer or a subsequent turn. For simple lookups, caching and pre-compiled agents reduce latency. We can show patterns from existing customers.
[06:40] Marco: security — SOC2, ISO, logs, SSO. do you offer audit log exports?
[06:46] Jenna: yes, audit logs and retention tiers are available as an add-on. We provide SOC2 Type II reports to enterprise and SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning; Dedicated and Private give you more control over log retention and export paths.
[07:05] Liam: ok. what's the expected cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for similar throughput?
[07:10] Jenna: ballpark: Hosted is higher per-token for peak but no infra commitments; Dedicated has committed monthly cost but lower unit cost and predictable throughput. Exact numbers depend on model family, quantization, and context window; we'll send a modeled spreadsheet with scenarios.
[07:30] Priya: for benchmarking — we want to compare 3 models on: answer quality (factuality+instruction-following), multilingual correctness, latency at p50/p95, and token cost. Also run a tool-calling robustness test.
[07:45] Samir: perfect. For bench infra we'll need sample prompts, expected flow traces, and a small test corpus in spanish/pt/en. Also define success criteria — e.g., quality delta acceptable under 5% vs gold for core tasks.
[08:05] Priya: success criteria: 1) >=90% quality on triage tasks, 2) p95 < 800ms for chat queries (no huge context), 3) function-call success rate >98%. For deep summarization >60k tokens we'll accept higher latencies.
[08:28] Liam: any limitations on embeddings/semantic search integration? we use FAISS and want to keep vector store in our VPC.
[08:36] Samir: no problem — you can keep vector store in your infra; Redwood will call retrieval endpoints over VPC peering and you can control caching and tokenization. We'll provide guidance on hybrid reranking and rerank policies.
[08:55] Marco: one more on compliance — are you able to commit to EU data residency? we have EU customers and can't send PII out.
[09:02] Jenna: yes, Dedicated or Private with EU region capacity will keep data in-region; we can show region-specific runbooks and contractual addenda.
[09:20] Liam: fine. let's talk about rollout — pilot size and timelines. we want a pilot for 3 weeks with 3 models and a small live set of traffic.
[09:29] Samir: timeline: week 0 — infra prep + seed dataset; week 1 — pilot deploy + smoke tests; week 2 — perf run and tuning; week 3 — evaluation and go/no-go. We'll support with an SE and an infra runbook.
[09:45] Priya: regarding tokenization — some Llama-derivatives have tokenization mismatches for portuguese; will you surface tokenization stats in the perf sheet?
[09:53] Samir: yes, perf sheet includes tokenization delta, char->token ratios per language, and cost estimates.
[10:05] Jenna: (interruption) quick housekeeping: i'll send pricing, samir will send bench plan, priya will share dataset, and marco will loop in infra/security contacts.
[10:18] Marco: sounds good.
[10:22] Samir: any concerns about model license / use-case restrictions?
[10:27] Priya: we prefer permissive L2 licenses, nothing that blocks commercial use or requires onerous model card constraints.
[10:34] Samir: understood — we'll prioritize Apache/MIT-like licensed weights; otherwise we'll show tradeoffs.
[10:43] Liam: earlier you mentioned streaming — for long summarization, do you recommend chunked generation or a single long-context pass?
[10:52] Samir: depends. For >64k, chunked with retrieval and partial synthesis often beats one giant pass for both cost and latency; but for strict coherency sometimes single-pass with large-context models is preferable. We'll include both patterns in the bench.
[11:12] Priya: what's the process for private air-gap install? we have an internal ops team and they will want the RPMs or docker images.
[11:20] Samir: we provide an air-gapped bundle with images, an install guide, and an operator support window. Private deployments have optional managed support from Redwood.
[11:35] Jenna: ok let's capture next steps — I'll recap.
[11:40] Jenna: next steps: i) i'll email pricing and perf sheet by march 10, ii) samir will share a 3-model benchmark plan by march 12, iii) priya will upload sample prompts/dataset by march 11, iv) schedule pilot kickoff week of march 15. Anything to add?
[11:58] Liam: please include the EU residency and SOC2 docs in the packet.
[12:04] Marco: and a sample VPC design + KMS integration example.
[12:09] Jenna: will do. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and set the kickoff.
[12:16] (call ends)
